title: Month 14
subtitle: Words are coming. The fifteen-month visit is next month, and it is the one where language gets counted.

baby.development: Your child is walking well, climbing onto low furniture, and can say several words. They point at what they want and look back at you to check you saw it.

you.body: Your back and knees are doing more work than they did a year ago. Lifting a walking child is a different movement than lifting a baby.
you.mind: Fourteen months is when the child starts to have a plan. It is also when the house needs a second look, because they can now reach things they could not last month.

coreActions.title: Book the fifteen-month visit
coreActions.why: This is the next vaccine set and the visit where the doctor counts words and watches the child walk.
coreActions.detail: The US schedule at fifteen months is DTaP, Hib, PCV, MMR, varicella, and hepatitis A and B depending on what was given earlier. Write down the words the child says so you can answer the question accurately.

coreActions.title: Count the words, and write them down
coreActions.why: A list of the words your child says is the single most useful thing you can bring to the fifteen-month visit.
coreActions.detail: At fifteen months, most children say a few words beyond mama and dada. They do not have to be clear. Write down every word you have heard, including the ones only you understand, and bring the list.

coreActions.title: Get shoes that bend
coreActions.why: A stiff shoe changes how a new walker moves, and a new walker is still learning the movement.
coreActions.detail: The shoe should bend where the foot bends, have a thin sole, and leave room at the toe. Check the fit every two months, because toddler feet grow in bursts. Bare feet indoors is still better.

alsoKnow.title: Pointing is a language milestone
alsoKnow.body: Pointing at something and looking back at you is a shared-attention skill, and it comes before words. A child who does not point by eighteen months is worth mentioning at the visit.

alsoKnow.title: Climbing starts before you expect it
alsoKnow.body: A child who can walk can usually climb onto a low chair. Anchor the furniture, and move the things you do not want reached one shelf higher than you think is necessary.

redFlags.text: Choking — cannot breathe, cough, or make a sound
A fall from a height, or a head injury with vomiting or unusual sleepiness
A fever over 100.4°F with unusual sleepiness or a rash
